name: Microarchitectural timing attacks (Spectre, DrawnApart, cache side channels)
plain: Uses precise timing to read CPU cache or GPU execution quirks.
meaning: Browser JS can run cache side channels (prime+probe), Spectre variants and GPU timing fingerprints (DrawnApart, 2022) that identify a physical GPU by execution unit speeds. Defended by timer coarsening and site isolation.

web.api: performance.now(), SharedArrayBuffer clocks, WebGL/WebGPU timer queries

limits.headline: Can use very exact timing to learn how your processor or graphics chip behaves
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page runs, and it takes many tries
can: Run tests that time your processor cache
Use graphics timing to tell apart physical chips, as the DrawnApart research did in 2022
Add the result to a device profile
cannot: Work well if the browser blurs the clock
Directly open your files or passwords in modern browsers
Know who you are by itself

story.what_it_is: A script uses precise timing to read CPU cache or GPU behavior and could leak hidden data or identity.

marketing.name: Why COOP and COEP
marketing.pitch: Google explains that browsers added isolation and coarser timers because of Spectre style timing attacks.

story.for_you: You never see it. After the Spectre discovery, browsers blurred their clocks and walled sites off from each other. These changes protect you from timing attacks that could read secrets.
story.for_makers: For attackers, timing can show what the chip is doing, even across sites. For makers, it means browsers will limit precise timers unless a site proves it is isolated. Researchers also show it can identify specific chips.

use_cases.example: Researchers show that a web page could use timing to read data it should not see, which led to Spectre defenses.
A tracker could use GPU timing as a hardware fingerprint, as shown in the DrawnApart research.
A browser game that needs fast threads must now opt in to cross origin isolation to get precise timers.
A bank site is kept apart from other tabs so a bad page cannot time its way into reading balances.
Browser makers make timers coarser, then give them back only to isolated pages.
A company runs a strict browser policy that isolates its web apps from untrusted pages.
A university security class demos a timing attack in a lab to teach why timers are blurred.

technical_bounds: Largely mitigated by Site Isolation and clock coarsening
Research prototypes, not seen in typical fingerprinting scripts

value.abuse: Cross-origin data leaks, stable GPU identification

history.change: Spectre mitigations: timer clamping, site isolation (Chrome 67, Firefox 100 Fission)
DrawnApart (Laor et al., NDSS 2022) shows 98% GPU re-identification in 8 s

refs.label: Oren et al., Spy in the Sandbox (CCS 2015)
